title: Broadcom Holds Early Talks About Financing Deal for OpenAI Chips
source_used: The Business Times (Singapore), which credits the Wall Street Journal
key_facts: Broadcom is arranging more than $50 billion in financing for the custom AI chip it is developing with OpenAI, the Wall Street Journal reported.
Apollo Global Management and Blackstone are among the lenders in talks, citing unidentified people familiar with the discussions.
Oracle is also talking to Apollo and Goldman Sachs to line up money for its chip purchases.
The companies are seeking the deals because of soaring costs to outfit data centres.

Broadcom said in June it had set up a platform, with Apollo and Blackstone as anchor investors, to help finance more than 20 gigawatts of AI computing for developers including Anthropic and OpenAI through 2028.
quote_evidence: Broadcom is arranging more than US$50 billion in financing for the custom artificial intelligence chip it is developing with OpenAI, part of a surge in deals to pay for AI infrastructure, the Wall Street Journal reported.
Apollo Global Management and Blackstone are among the lenders in talks to participate in the deal, the Journal said, citing unidentified people familiar with the discussions.
why_it_matters_hint: A large debt package would fund AI chip capacity for OpenAI, but the talks are early and rest on unnamed sources.
